note: Published Massachusetts program rates. The conversions to a price per kWh are ours, and each says so.

sources.statewide_plan: 2025-2027 Statewide Plan, Exhibit 1, Figures 29 and 39, D.P.U. 24-140 to 24-149, as read by the Boston Energy Atlas: https://bostonenergyatlas.org/entity#decision:connectedsolutions
sources.home_battery_materials: Massachusetts residential battery program materials, 13 Mar 2026: https://www.capelightcompact.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/ma_resi_battery_program_materials-3-13-26_CLEAN.pdf
sources.two_way_car: National Grid statement in Electrek, 23 Jul 2026: https://electrek.co/2026/07/23/massachusetts-ev-drivers-battery-power-v2g/
sources.managed_charging: Eversource managed charging page, read 5 Nov 2026; 2027 amounts pending: https://www.eversource.com/residential/save-money-energy/clean-energy-options/electric-vehicles/ev-charger-managed-charging

program.note: Neither the plan nor the March 2026 materials shows a winter rate. FlexGrid's own sale windows come from ISO-NE's real peak and stay as signed off.

event_price_basis: $275 per kW over 45 three-hour events, the middle of the program's 30 to 60. Our conversion. The market test's stand-in buyer pays this price.
coordinator_keeps_basis: Assumed: the old book's $220 net on $275. No published fee.

x_basis.home_battery: $275 less the coordinator's 20%. Two-way cars count here.
x_basis.building: $200 Daily Dispatch over $275, less 20%. A building's own battery counts here too.
x_basis.home_other: No per-kW rate exists. Real payments are $20 a thermostat and $120 a managed charger a year: $140 over the 1.97 kW these devices sell in a Tier 1 home is $71 per kW, then less 20%. Water heaters, appliances and pools have no real rate of their own.
